questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to be in the center of biotechnology, therefore  I choose to study in Boston. Also, it was important for me that it was an English speaking country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I feel that I got the full college experience, but there is I few things that I would have done differently

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, the most important information was sent to you in email before arrival, and Sage the coordinator was very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really receive assistance. I would have liked a specific welcome program for the exchange students before classes started. There were a couple of events but else you were let to yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were apartments, dorms with single rooms or shared. I knew that it would be too difficult to find housing on my own and I hoped that I could meet someone if I choose to live in a dorm. Many who live in dorms are freshmen which means that they are between 18 and 19 years old. Therefore I wish that I had chosen to live in an apartment-style even though it's more expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In dorms you eglibed to have a mealplan. The food in the dining halls is very American-inspired, so it was kinda boring and often unhealthy. But nice not to prepare any of the food yourself because your days will be packed. Most of the apartments have a kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Are you willing to share a small room with another person? If not try to contact other exchange students to find housing off-campus, or choose a single room in an apartment or the dorms

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it very old and expensive. Even though you live in a dorm there is nothing social. The apartments were nicer but more expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration was very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In April you could start register for classes and change and add classes until October. The website was kind of old, but easy to navigate.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The professors who taught the courses were very helpful about registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Many of the courses I wanted was already closed when I could register, but it was nice too add and drop courses until October.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the recommendations from other students before deciding. And, just choose the courses you find most interesting you can always drop them. Choose more than you should in case one of them is bad

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved the teachers, so passionate and helpful.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was lower than KU, but the workload was bigger.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You get points for your participation, which can be challenging sometimes, but the teachers were very helpful. The lectures were very much the same

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Developmental Biology
Introduction to Neuroscience
General Microbiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all my classes, especially Developmental Biology. The professor, Cynthia learned all of our names and was so passionate and smart. Even though it was the class with the heaviest material it was the lectures I enyojed the most. In Introduction Neuroscience, there is a lot of freshmen, but our guest lectures were very interesting. General Microbiology you have lab for two hours, twice a week. The workload for this course is big, but the material is straight forward, The work in the lab was sometimes a bit boring.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The mandatory health insurance is pretty expensive. I was surprised about how expensive the US is, restaurants, groceries... Don't buy the metro card to the T (the metro). You will not use it and buy a membership for the Bluebikes instead. Also in Boston you either walk to everything or take an Uber.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food! You have to tip 15-20 % each time you eat out which often will make it more expensive than eating out in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: SO many different clubs. Many Americans meet their friends through clubs so don't hesitate to join a sports club or an academic. You can visit the club at an event at the start of the semester. And forget to sign up for a sports class which is free! You can learn to ice skate, do yoga and many more.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The limit does not exist. Over 200 different clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the running club, where I met a lot of sweet Americans. Get to know Boston and visit Harvard and MIT. Look for local activities and explore the national holidays. Befriend an American and explore the culture.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is cheap! take the train to New York for a long weekend. Also make sure that your insurance cover renting a car and driving to New Hampshire, Maine, or Cape Cod for hiking. The Amtrak train can also take you to nice neighboring cities like Providence.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy! Americans are very friendly! But it takes some work to get close to them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs! And talk to your classmates! Many of them don't know one either. Always say yes for social events outside class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Americans are very good at first impression but it takes some work to really befriend them. I found it easier to get friends with the other exchange students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very friendly and easy to talk to. The people were more open.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Focus on the social in the start, this is where you find your friends. Join some clubs. And be open-minded.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress over the classes, most often you will have three exams spread over the semester which enables you to keep track of how it goes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to make unique friendships with people all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find "your people". You have to do a great effort to find your friends, and get out of your comfort zone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Try to get some scholarships before arrival

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
